result:
I fixed F-DG2-500. A session that ends while the sign-in page is shown now clears the cache, and the next person to sign in in that tab no longer sees the previous user's records. Every required check ran in both locale settings. The only non-zero exit is `pnpm format:check` (exit 2), caused by sandbox-masked dotfiles; the `--ignore-path` variant exits 0. Nothing is committed. The handback is `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG2/T-DG2-FE13-frontend-ux-engineer.md`.

**The fix**
- **Clearing where the session ends:** the API client now clears the cached records itself at the moment a 401 ends the session, before any page can react. The app wires this up when it creates its `QueryClient` (`createQueryClient()`), so it no longer depends on `<RequireSession>` being mounted. That component now only navigates to the sign-in page.
- **Identity check:** every `/me` answer is compared with the last identity this tab saw (organization, user and session). If it differs, all cached records are removed before the new identity is stored, so nothing renders under it while the old data is still there. This covers a sign-in in another tab and Back/Forward, even when no 401 was ever seen.
- **Session subject:** `/me` has no session id, and adding one would mean editing `apps/api` or `packages/shared`, which were off-limits. I used the CSRF token instead, since the API derives it from the session token.
- **Draft forms:** when a different person signs in, the signed-in page is rebuilt, so A's unsaved form input doesn't carry over to B. If the same person signs in again elsewhere, records are refetched but their own unsaved input is kept. If you'd rather drop input on any session change, it's a one-line change in `session.tsx`, but it would also drop the "language not saved" notice in the existing 403 e2e test.
- **Unchanged:** sign-out in this tab clears everything as before. The existing session-end tests (12 unit, 8 e2e) still pass, so one landing on sign-in, bounded `/me` requests and "a 403 is never a session end" all still hold.

The handback has the full cache sweep: React Query records and submitted form values, the CSRF token, session state, component state, and `localStorage`. I deliberately kept the language choice and table column settings in `localStorage`; they hold no record data. Nothing in the app uses `sessionStorage`.

**Tests**
- **Unit:** 18 new tests in `session-identity.test.tsx`, in EN and AR. They cover the reviewer's W5 and W5b, an identity change via a refocus `/me`, sign-out here, a 403 not being an end, and clearing with nothing mounted.
- **Reviewer's probe:** 26/26 pass on the fix (W5 and W5b: `B sees A's row=false`). That was a development run; I didn't keep its log.
- **e2e:** a new real-stack test in `session-end.spec.ts`, in EN and AR. User A sees a Finance record, the session ends while the sign-in page is shown, and user B signs in in the same tab. B's list request is held for 1.5 s, and a page observer confirms A's record never appears in B's view.
- **Negative controls on `HEAD`:**
  - Unit: 14 of 18 fail. On `HEAD`, A's records stay cached and B sees A's row. The 4 that pass are the sign-out and same-identity guards, which `HEAD` already handled.
  - e2e: both fail. A's record entered B's page on the real stack.

**Checks** (unset and `C.UTF-8`, same result in both)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| typecheck, build, lint | exit 0 |
| `pnpm test`, Node 22 and Node 24 | 866 passed (FE12's 848 plus my 18) |
| contrast | PASS |
| e2e (P1, P2, `p2-blank-text`, `session-end`; EN and AR) | 70 passed |
| axe | 266 scans, 0 violations of any impact |
| `validate.mjs --historical --stage DG1` | PASS |
| `pnpm format:check` | exit 2: 12 unreadable files the sandbox masks, not repo content; Prettier says all files are formatted, and the `--ignore-path` variant exits 0 |

The only warnings in the logs are ones earlier handbacks also report: a Fastify deprecation from an API test, Vite's chunk-size note, and `npm warn` lines. There are no React warnings and no hook timeouts.

**Gaps:** W5b (sign-in at the identity provider in another tab) isn't reproduced in a real browser, because the test stack runs in dev sign-in mode with no identity provider; the unit test covers it. The e2e test returns to the earlier sign-in page with `history.go(-2)`, which is equivalent to choosing that entry from the Back button's history list.

Evidence is in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG2/T-DG2-FE13-evidence/`. It has every check log for both modes, both negative-control logs, the axe summaries and the two cited screenshots:
- `en-user-a-sees-record.png`
- `ar-user-b-never-sees-a.png`
